sent_subject: Sproutbox quiz→box→checkout: 5 ranked tests + ad angles
sent:
Mira—

Here’s the blunt version you asked for: five ranked tests for your quiz→box builder→checkout, each with example Meta angles to ship in parallel. No fluff.

Track these checkpoints as you test
- quiz_start, quiz_complete, builder_start, first_add, box_complete, checkout_start, purchase.

1) Q1 start friction and promise clarity
Hypothesis: people hesitate at the first screen when the value isn’t concrete and the effort looks long.
Try:
- Keep the ad’s promise in the headline; add a short expectation line (“Takes a minute”).
- Show progress (“Step 1 of 4”).
- Move any email gate to after a results preview.
Measure: starts→completes; lift to builder_start.
Ad angles (ship 3): UGC “I answered 3 questions and it built my week” demo; founder explainer to camera; progress‑bar motion graphic.

2) Quiz sequencing and scope—lead with taste, compress to essentials
Hypothesis: early commitment/lifestyle questions create drop; taste/diet is the hook.
Try:
- Lead with taste/diet; keep to 3–4 essentials; move non‑essentials into the builder.
- Show a live “building your picks” strip beneath the quiz as answers are made.
- Email gate only after a results preview with 3 suggestions visible.
Measure: completion rate; CTR from results to builder_start.
Ad angles: “Pick your tastes. We’ll do the rest.” fast‑tap cuts; diet‑specific cuts (Vegetarian / High‑Protein / Family); “See your picks before you decide” demo.

3) Builder choice architecture—defaults, anchoring, fewer first choices
Hypothesis: blank‑slate builders stall; equal‑weight grids overload.
Try:
- Pre‑fill a Starter Box from the quiz with a clear “Swap” path.
- Offer 2–3 presets (Fast Start, Family, High‑Protein) alongside “Build from scratch.”
- Sticky tally with items, total and per‑meal price; limit initial visible choices to 6–8; use tabs (Quick / Kids / Protein).
- Nudge: “You’re 1 item away from a complete box.”
Measure: first_add rate; box_complete; AOV.
Ad angles: real‑time “watch me build a box” screen‑record; carousel of the 3 presets; persona UGC building their box.

4) Pricing and delivery clarity—surface early
Hypothesis: late price/delivery info creates leaks at checkout.
Try:
- Show an all‑in estimated total on the builder that updates live.
- If you use a free‑delivery threshold, show progress toward it in the sticky bar.
- Let people pick delivery day earlier (end of builder or first checkout step).
- Compact trust cluster near totals (security icons, simple skip/returns promise).
Measure: builder→checkout_start; checkout_start→purchase.
Ad angles: “No surprises at checkout” overlay on builder; “Choose your delivery day” cut; static close‑up with “Price you see is the price you pay.”

5) Checkout friction—remove the pauses
Hypothesis: extra fields and code hunting kill momentum.
Try:
- Offer express checkout options above the fold.
- Address autocomplete; postcode first.
- Move discount code behind a link; one clear order summary with thumbnails.
- Reassurance microcopy next to the final CTA (dispatch timing, skip/cancel policy if applicable).
Measure: checkout_start→purchase; median checkout duration.
Ad angles: “From box to checkout in one screen” demo; clean order‑summary static with “No faff.”

Creative cadence while you run the tests
- For the top two tests, ship three variants per concept this week; same next week for the next two tests. Our three‑week rule: retire creative after ~three weeks of falling click‑through; every concept ships in at least three variants so the account can learn.
